title: CMake local install RPATH missing
author: Ryanf55
body:
I tried consuming a locally installed version of MAVSDK in another package's install, and MAVSDK's CMake target fails to correctly export the shared library destination on an installed target.
I suspected this is an rpath issue, and spent 2 hours trying various recommendations, but have not found a solution.
Here is a conference talk from a CMake maintainer specifically about this use case with rpath:
https://youtu.be/m0DwB4OvDXk?si=3TaOFA6OdxY4z5F6&t=2452

I tried his recommendation on MAVSDK, and that did not fix the issue.

To reproduce, here's a Dockerfile:

```docker
FROM ubuntu:22.04

WORKDIR /ws

# https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build_linux.html

RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        python3 \
        python3-pip

RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
# Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install


RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        pkg-config \
        astyle \
        bluez \
        bluez-tools \
        libbluetooth-dev

WORKDIR /ws
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules --branch cmake-install https://github.com/ryanf55/RemoteIDTransmitter.git
WORKDIR /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter
RUN CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/ws/MAVSDK/install cmake -B build
RUN cmake --build build
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter
```

Just run `docker build . --progress=plain` and you will eventually get 
```
 > [stage-0 17/17] RUN ./install/bin/rid-transmitter:
0.378 ./install/bin/rid-transmitter: error while loading shared libraries: libmavsdk.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The example here is when I tried using an installed executable that links to MAVSDK.
The linkage to MAVSDK is using the standard target_link_libraries approach:
https://github.com/Ryanf55/RemoteIDTransmitter/blob/cmake-install/CMakeLists.txt#L37


FYI @dakejahl

comments.body:
> ```
> # Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
> RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
> ```

Why? Isn't this the root cause? Why can't you use the `--target install` as it is intended?

> > ```
> > # Install is slightly different not using the install target, but it's the same idea.
> > RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
> > ```
> 
> Why? Isn't this the root cause? Why can't you use the `--target install` as it is intended?

No, you get the same error, the only difference is one allows you to set the install location at install time, while the other requires to decide during configure time. For this example, it has no effect.

First, a quick fix: you can set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`:

```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/ ./install/bin/rid-transmitter
```

> I tried his recommendation on MAVSDK, and that did not fix the issue.

What did you try? Note that I didn't watch the video.

I would be tempted to try something like this:

```patch
diff --git a/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt b/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt
index 6392ba41..73f6194e 100644
--- a/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -130,10 +130,19 @@ else()
     )
 endif()
 
+if(IS_ABSOLUTE "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
+    set(MAVSDK_INSTALL_RPATH "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
+else()
+    set(MAVSDK_INSTALL_RPATH "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
+endif()
+
 set_target_properties(mavsdk PROPERTIES
     VERSION ${MAVSDK_VERSION_STRING}
     SOVERSION ${MAVSDK_SOVERSION_STRING}
+    INSTALL_RPATH "${MAVSDK_INSTALL_RPATH}"
+    INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH TRUE
 )
+
 if (MSVC)
     set_target_properties(mavsdk PROPERTIES
         DEBUG_POSTFIX "d"
```

Now if I build it with:

```
cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=install -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
cmake --build build --target install
```

Then the rpath is correct and it works with your `rid-transmitter`:

```
# readelf -d /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2 | grep RUNPATH
 0x000000000000001d (RUNPATH)            Library runpath: [/ws/MAVSDK/install/lib]
```

The problem with your `cmake --install build --prefix install` is then that it sets the install path at install time, though the rpath is set at build time. So the way you call it, it would result in the wrong rpath anyway, because my patch above relies on `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`.

```
# readelf -d /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2 | grep RUNPATH
 0x000000000000001d (RUNPATH)            Library runpath: [/usr/local/lib]
```

Now one may argue that it is good enough to have it set with `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX`, and if you really need to change the install path at install time with `--prefix`, then you can manually set the rpath with something like:

```
patchelf --set-rpath /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2
```

Or set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.

@Ryanf55: what do you think? Does that correspond to what your video says? Maybe there is a better way that works with setting the `--prefix` at install time, but my guess is that CMake won't go change the binary at this step, so it's too late to change the runpath.

I actually watched the video you linked above, and it is a very nice presentation 😊. However, I don't think that setting the rpath to $ORIGIN will solve this particular problem you have. It would help MAVSDK find its own dependencies, but in your case the problem is about `rid-transmitter` not finding MAVSDK.

When you have your issue, the `ldd` output looks like this:

```
# ldd install/bin/rid-transmitter 
	linux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007fe0137ef000)
	libmavsdk.so.3 => not found
	libbluetooth.so.3 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libbluetooth.so.3 (0x00007fe013753000)
	libstdc++.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 (0x00007fe013400000)
	libm.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6 (0x00007fe01366c000)
	libgcc_s.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgcc_s.so.1 (0x00007fe01364c000)
	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007fe013000000)
	/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 (0x00007fe0137f1000)
```

It could build against MAVSDK, but at runtime the dynamic linker doesn't know where to find it because libmavsdk.so.3 did not have a runpath set and is installed in a custom location.

My understanding is that the $ORIGIN trick would help your executable. Maybe it's easier to show with an example. You have this issue:

```sh
# ./install/bin/rid-transmitter 
./install/bin/rid-transmitter: error while loading shared libraries: libmavsdk.so.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

Say you copy `libmavsdk.so.3` next to `rid-transmitter` and set the runpath to $ORIGIN, then it will work:

```
# cp /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3 /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter/install/bin/
# patchelf --set-rpath '$ORIGIN' /ws/RemoteIDTransmitter/install/bin/rid-transmitter

# ./install/bin/rid-transmitter 
Parsing failed:
File could not be opened for reading
	(error occurred at line 0, column 0 of '/root/.local/share/rid-transmitter/config.toml')
```

I am assuming that the "Parsing failed" error is orthogonal to the dynamic linking issue we're discussing now 🙈.

So you can use $ORIGIN in order to find dependencies next to your binary, but setting it into your dependencies won't help you in this case.

What about these three workarounds:

1. Install into `/usr`:

```
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr
RUN cmake --build build -j8
RUN cmake --build build --target install
```

2. Install into `/usr/local` (which is the cmake default):

```
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
RUN cmake --build build --target install
```

3. Install using wget/dpkg

```
RUN --mount=target=/var/lib/apt/lists,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    --mount=target=/var/cache/apt,type=cache,sharing=locked \
    apt-get update && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y install \
        build-essential \
        cmake \
        git \
        wget

RUN wget https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v3.10.2/libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_ubuntu22.04_amd64.deb
RUN dpkg -i libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_ubuntu22.04_amd64.deb
```

> What about these three workarounds

Those will work because they install MAVSDK on the system. I think the original issue is that they want to install MAVSDK locally and use it from there.

The more I think about it, the more I believe that the solution is to either use LD_LIBRARY_PATH or manually `patchelf`:

```
RUN git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
WORKDIR /ws/MAVSDK
RUN git submodule update --init --recursive

RUN cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild -S.
RUN cmake --build build -j8
RUN cmake --install build --prefix install
patchelf --set-rpath /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib /ws/MAVSDK/install/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.10.2
```

Because MAVSDK cannot guess the final use-case and should probably not leak paths of the build machine. The package knows how it will be used and can set the runpath after installation (with `patchelf --set-rpath`).
There was no more follow up. I assume this is good enough and I'm closing this. Please comment again if I'm wrong.

author: weagle08
body:
MAVSDK version v1.4.4
PX4 v12.3

When I execute a get_all_params against the mavsdk::Param plugin I am getting a seg fault on a different thread immediately after trying to access any of the vectors of the mavsdk::Param::AllParams returned value. I'm doing the request after successfully connecting to a PX4 flight controller. I'm new to MAVSDK and mavlink in general so any assistance in tracking this down would be appreciated.

instead of passing back a copy of the _all_params list, the actual list is returned and so when I access it on a different thread I think this is where the seg fault happens?

Amazing, thank you for the example! I'll try to tackle it this week.

I think the line you mentioned is not great indeed but I don't think that's the reason because in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/v1.4/src/mavsdk/plugins/param/param_impl.cpp#L68 it creates a copy.

These:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1788/commits/812fa0a94c9871b1e032cdb3c35cd1bb8ead08bf
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1788/commits/5ce3a5c2c821e5273c09a56ecf719eb5b36d52df

Now here comes the funny part. I just tried your example and couldn't reproduce it. I assume it depends on the PX4 version as well. I tested against PX4 `main`. I'll get back to this later.

Yes, you're right. It's definitely caused by double fulfillment of the timeout callback. That is odd that you could not reproduce the issue. I've only tested against PX4 running in a docker container. I'll try against actual hardware (CUBE H7 Blue) as soon as I can and post the result).

I also tried against PX4 SITL v1.12.3 and it works just fine.

My best guess is that you link against some MAVSDK .so file on your system that you're not aware of. It might be worthwhile to remove anything installed system-wide in `/usr` and `/usr/local`:

```
sudo apt remove libmavsdk-dev
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/include/mavsdk /usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so /usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.* /usr/local/lib/cmake/MAVSDK
```

I do not utilize a locally installed version of MAVSDK. I build in the same manner as the project I posted, so it does a full build of mavsdk and links against the static lib that gets output. I'll keep looking at this as I'm very curious how the callback is even being hit twice because I see the lock guards and the checks for callback being null. Will report anything I find, but may be a couple weeks.

I'm going to close this since I seem to be the only one that's had this issue. I haven't had a chance to address it since using a passthrough subscription for params is fine for what I'm doing for now. and if it's a non-issue I don't want it sitting open. If someone else sees the problem they'll open a new issue I'm sure.

drone = System()
await drone.connect(system_address="__input_addres__")

linked_prs.title: telemetry: Use REQUEST_DATA_STREAM for ArduPilot set_rate

comments.body:
Hello @julianoes ,
Is this issue open for contribution? I am a first-time contributor and would be happy to work on it if you could assign it to me.
@lakhmanisahil sure go ahead and make a pull request if you have a solution for it. I'm not working on it at the moment.
Thanks, @julianoes . I am looking into this issue and will aim to submit a PR.

Hi @julianoes, I've been studying the source (no hardware yet) and I think the fix should go inside `telemetry_impl.cpp`. All the `set_rate_xxx` functions call `_system_impl->set_msg_rate()` / `set_msg_rate_async()`, which internally send `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` (cmd 511) — ArduPilot doesn't ACK this reliably on serial links. 

I can see `_system_impl->effective_autopilot()` is already used in `process_sys_status()`, so the fix would be to check `effective_autopilot() == Autopilot::ArduPilot` and fall back to `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM` instead for the affected rate setters. 

Planning to open a PR regarding this. Does that approach look right to you?

Files I'd change: [`telemetry_impl.cpp`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.cpp) · [`telemetry_impl.h`](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/cpp/src/mavsdk/plugins/telemetry/telemetry_impl.h)

Investigated the ArduPilot source — `MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL` is fully supported for both `ATTITUDE` and `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT`. The command is correctly handled, ACKed, and applied.

The actual root cause is **GCS stream rate override**: when another GCS application (MAVProxy, QGC, Mission Planner) on the same MAVLink link sends `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM`, ArduPilot's `initialise_message_intervals_for_stream()` overwrites all individual message intervals in that stream group. So the rate set by MAVSDK gets silently clobbered.

Confirmed by ArduPilot issues: ArduPilot/ardupilot#17046, ArduPilot/ardupilot#19761, ArduPilot/ardupilot#28550.

**Workarounds:**
- Set `MAVn_OPTIONS` bit 2 (NOSTREAMOVERRIDE) on the ArduPilot port used by MAVSDK
- Ensure no other GCS sends `REQUEST_DATA_STREAM` on the same link
- When using SITL with MAVProxy, start with `--streamrate=-1`

This is not a MAVSDK bug — it's a user configuration issue on the ArduPilot side.
Oh, this makes more sense. Thanks for investigating @PavelGuzenfeld. I'll close this issue then.

title: UDP reconnect logic with PX4
author: al2950
body:
I think this issue has probably caught a few people out in the past. But when using UDP with PX4, PX4 will record the port & ip address of the first heartbeat it receives. It will then send any status and responses to this address. This address is set once, and only once, and so if you disconnect and reconnect with a different local port (on client), you will not receive any messages until the PX4 is rebooted.

Suggest adding a default port to MavSDK which it attempts to bind to, currently it is set to 0 so OS picks a 'sensible' random port.

comments.body: Isn't that a PX4 issue? If PX4 only supports one UDP client and needs to be rebooted to move to a new one, then it has to be fixed on the PX4 side, doesn't it?
One thing to note is that PX4 re-uses the same ports, so they are both set statically, while MAVSDK chooses the local port randomly.

> Isn't that a PX4 issue? If PX4 only supports one UDP client and needs to be rebooted to move to a new one, then it has to be fixed on the PX4 side, doesn't it?

Maybe, but I dont think its a bug in PX4.

Firstly (in PX4) most of the logic assumes a single client, allowing multiple clients would add complexity (which in turn decreases reliability)  Secondly adding logic to monitor a client, and potentially drop it if it does not hear from it may result in unintended dropped clients due to a network hitch... which would be a safety concern. 

I have not discussed this on the PX4 github, but my pov was that it would be way easier to just allow a user to specify a local port with MAVSDK. If not then i suggest adding this note to the troubleshooting docs

Disclaimer: I am not the one who needs to be convinced, I'll leave the final word to Julian 😇. But I'd like to share my opinion, which is that PX4 having to reboot in order to swap to a different client is a bug. And allowing to set the local port with MAVSDK would be a hack. The way I see client-server connections is that the server exposes a port and the client contacts it over this port. When I connect to GitHub, my browser does not set a local port to make it easier for GitHub to answer, and I don't need to reboot GitHub between two calls 🙈.

This said, without changing anything, I'm pretty sure that you can solve your problem with mavlink-router. Did you consider that?

I agree with @JonasVautherin but I'm also aware that we can't just change the way PX4 is set up, and we want to be compatible with it, so we should find a way.

title: GTest is a submodule dependency, but unless all other dependencies is not automatically downloaded
author: LorenzMeier
body:
This leads to unexpected build failures on clean checkouts:

```
CMake Error at src/CMakeLists.txt:73 (add_subdirectory):
  The source directory

    /Users/lorenzmeier/src/MAVSDK/src/third_party/gtest

  does not contain a CMakeLists.txt file.
```

Running `git submodule init && git submodule update` fixes it. Having some dependencies auto-download and others not is very confusing.

comments.body:
That's an interesting point. I would believe that this is one consequence of using submodules: you can never really know if you must fetch the submodules or if they are optional, can you?

The reasoning is the following:
* For some reasons we could discuss, I am not into using submodules for dependencies.
* When I moved the dependencies into a superbuild, I did not change gtest. Because we need submodules for `proto/` and `mavlink/`, that would not have removed the need for a `--recursive` checkout. I am not sure if moving gtest into our superbuild would make sense or not. I guess it could, because the [Google note](https://github.com/google/googletest/blob/36066cfecf79267bdf46ff82ca6c3b052f8f633c/googletest/docs/faq.md#why-is-it-not-recommended-to-install-a-pre-compiled-copy-of-google-test-for-example-into-usrlocal) advising against installing gtest may apply to other dependencies, and therefore one should probably not install dependencies coming from our superbuild.

TL;DR: we could move gtest into the superbuild, but that would not remove the need for the `--recursive` checkout.

What do you think? @julianoes do you have an opinion on that?

What I'm asking for is consistency: Either the super build handles all the dependencies, or it handles none and they are documented. I think removing the automation you already have would however be a mistake. It makes it convenient. If you simply add the git submodules update to the super build you're already done.

I wouldn't spend too much energy on trying to find the perfect solution. Do it one way, make it consistent and make sure the documentation is clear.

Right now my main criticism of the documentation is that it is trying to explain too much from the start (it is a reference, not a Quickstart). I don't want to read all of it. I just need to know if a) MAVSDK is for me (why should I use it) and b) give me the shell commands to get going in 3 minutes and c) give me a simple example.

That should be in the Quickstart and maybe even in the README. Look at what Homebrew does:
https://brew.sh

While I perfectly agree with you about the documentation, I don't think I would want the superbuild to update the submodules. Sometimes I want to test with different states of the submodules (`mavlink/` and/or `proto/`).

We could add logic similar to PX4, which shows a message to the user ("your submodules are not in the state we expect. If you're not an expert, type 'key', ..."). But this brings its own kind of complexity and confusion (which may be necessary for PX4, but which I believe is not for MAVSDK).

I would vote for merging that with #949 and I'll work on improving the documentation, if that's okay for you.
Cool.
Closing in favor of #949.

title: Set drone yaw in a MissionItem
author: depauwjimmy
body:
I have been trying Mission lately to take exactly the same picture again automatically.
It seems to work fine except for the drone yaw which changes somewhat randomly.
There is no option in MissionItem for me to specify a yaw or anything close to an orientation to make sure both him and the gimbal are facing the same way as the photo before.

Is it intentional ? How can i be sure to orient the camera exactly like when the first photo was taken?

Thanks for you insight

comments.body:
Looking at [MissionItem](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/develop/en/api_reference/classmavsdk_1_1_mission_item.html) it seems you are correct - it has gimbal yaw, but not vehicle yaw (which may differ).
@julianoes any reason not to support setting ROI too?

----

That said, this should not be "somewhat random". The way this works in MAVLink is that the [waypoint-like-items](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT) have a yaw field. If the yaw is explicitly specified then that will be used. If the yaw is a NaN the vehicle will point towards whatever the system setting is (that is set using parameters, and default to "the next waypoint". 
The yaw can also be affected by the gimbal and ROI. 

If you were working in raw mavlink then I'd suggest calling the command to set an ROI. Not sure what to do now, but Julian probably will be!

@hamishwillee so this would be for vehicles without gimbals which literally have to turn to take a picture? I have many open question when it comes to ROI, modes of yaw during a mission, gimbal ROI, etc. To me it sounds like you need to be lucky in combining all these things to get it to work, and with MAVSDK we try to hide that sort of complexity and give you something (and sometimes only one thing) that works.
So yes it would be nice to support all this but we need understand all these aspects.

I guess the 'somewhat random' is yaw toward waypoint right now since the movement is always the same. I just had no idea what was the referential.
It's totally not helping me though, i really need to control the yaw by myself in code.

I am not sure I understand the use-case :confused:. Right now, you can control the yaw of the camera, which works, while the drone will always keep looking at the next waypoint. Correct?

And you would like to be able to control both the yaw of the gimbal and the yaw of the drone, for some reason?

The gimbal yaw is not really used, we mostly need it for pitch changes and maybe roll later.
Our drone has other sensors and stuff pointing forward which are not on the gimbal. Instead of overloading the gimbal with too much stuff we find it a lot easier to control the drone yaw.
I could offset the gimbal so its facing the same thing as before but i have no idea what the drone yaw will be when reaching the waypoint so i can't give a good value when creating the mission item.
I believe this issue overlaps entirely with [issue #909](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/909).
Ok, let's close this one then. @depauwjimmy: feel free to reopen if you believe it is a different issue :blush:.

title: Issue of Mission Execution and Manual Input Priority
author: liu12344321
body:
When the "manual_control.set_manual_control_input"s value keeps changing, I want to execute a mission or other automode. In such a case, the value needs to remain consistent before and after the mission is triggered; otherwise, the mission will be interrupted. However, I’ve noticed that even if I set the manual value right before executing the mission, and then immediately trigger the task, it still gets interrupted. It turns out that I have to wait several hundred milliseconds after setting the value before executing the mission. It seems that the mission has a higher priority, even if the command is input later, the flight controller receives and processes it first.

Then I looked into the source code and found that these two types of commands follow different paths，one goes through a queue, while the other is sent directly as a command. So now I’m wondering: how can I make the information in the queue be delivered faster, so that I don’t have to wait for several hundred milliseconds?

Im current using v3.3.0
Thanks.

comments.body: I'm not following. What are you trying to do and what is the problem exactly? And is this with PX4 or ArduPilot?

@julianoes Im using PX4.
I want to implement the following use case: the drone is originally flying in mission mode, and my onboard vision computer monitors the environment. When an obstacle is detected, it will intervene and interrupt the mission. Once the obstacle is cleared and it's safe to proceed, I want to resume the mission.

The problem lies in resuming the mission. For example, initially I send set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 1, 0) to take control. Then, when I want to hand control back to the mission, I set set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 0.5, 0) and immediately call mission.start_mission(). After that, I continuously send set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 0.5, 0).

However, the resumed mission gets interrupted again right away. I believe this is because the earlier manual control input set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 1, 0) is still considered active by the flight controller. To avoid this, I have to wait a few hundred milliseconds after sending the first set_manual_control_input(0, 0, 0.5, 0) before calling mission.start_mission().

It seems like mission.start_mission() is being sent after but received before the manual control command by the flight controller.

Ok, I think manual_control is not the right interface to do this. Instead, I would pause the mission using `mission_pause` which will go into hold.

Or, alternatively if you want to do some control to avoid the obstacle, I would do that in offboard mode, e.g. using velocity commands.

Manual control is really meant for "manual" as in human control, and not automated control like that.

Also, PX4 implements an interface for obstacle avoidance that we probably should use instead, however, it's not implemented by MAVSDK yet, and I also don't know what the state of it is in PX4, but I do know that it would be the right thing to do, at least long term.

title: [Discussion] How to set a parameter and reboot the vehicle for PX4 MAVSDK SITL Test
author: junwoo091400
body:
## What I want to do
I wanted to have the following feature on [MAVSDK Test](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/tree/main/test/mavsdk_tests) in PX4 SITL:
1. Set the parameter in PX4 (to set it to a non-default value)
2. Reboot the vehicle (Or start the vehicle directly with the modified parameter from the beginning)
3. Perform a SITL MAVSDK test with the vehicle that had the modified parameter when it booted up

The reason for this was for the [Payload delivery SITL test PR](https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/pull/20230), I needed a way to set the parameter and reboot the vehicle, in order to have the startup script recognize the non-default parameter to enable the `payload_deliverer` module, and start the module, which is necessary for payload delivery feature.

## Problem
Currently it seems like we can't arbitrarily set the parameter before booting up, neither can we reboot the vehicle in the SITL test function.

### Proposed Solutions
1. Have a way to reboot the vehicle after setting the parameter in the mavsdk sitl test pipeline
2. Have a way to load an arbitrary / modified parameter through MAVSDK interface for the drone

## Discussion 
If we want to support such feature, what would be the best way to implement it? Are there any other solutions? Would this be possible without modifying MAVSDK?

comments.body:
So the goal of the test is to check that the parameter is set correctly after reboot, but SITL resets the params when it boots, right?

I don't really see how this is related to MAVSDK, though :thinking:. It feels like you need SITL to persist the params (instead of resetting after reboot), and that's not how SITL does it, right?

1. From what I know there is not yet a way to reboot/restart PX4 from within PX4 in SITL but only externally via helper scripts. So for the PX4 mavsdk_tests you would have to script it there.
2. You can always load/get an arbitrary param from PX4. I think that part is not a problem.

Regarding your question: to me it sounds like a test script issue around PX4, and not a MAVSDK issue as such.

But then if it requires custom code to make it work in SITL, is it really a test? It feels like params persistence after reboot is just not a SITL feature. We can simulate it with external scripts, and then we can test that those external scripts simulate it correctly, but at the end of the day it's not testing the actual feature :sweat_smile:

I think I found the solution :thinking:, which is using a custom model with the airframe file specifying the parameters that needs to be changed on startup. It is of course not scalable, but for a SITL test for a specific feature, I think this can be tolerated.
